name: Cosmic Byte Artemis (04d9:a1ce) [provisional — does not work yet]
note: PROVISIONAL / NON-FUNCTIONAL. The whole `protocol` block below is still a verbatim copy of hive65.json and is WRONG for this board — it is kept only because the loader requires the keys to be present. This board is NOT in the SinoWealth 258a report-6 family: 04d9 is a Holtek MCU with a different transport, so the `standard` encoder cannot drive it and no JSON-only change will make it work. Read on hardware (2026-08-10, wired): the board exposes 4 HID interfaces and NONE of them declares a Report ID 6, so `desc_marker()` (b'\x85\x06') never matches and find_device() correctly ignores this profile rather than sending it bad frames. The vendor interface is the one on usage page 0xFF01 (/dev/hidraw6 in that session), whose descriptor is: Report Size 8, no Report ID at all, 64-byte Input (usage 0x20), 64-byte OUTPUT (usage 0x21), and only an 8-byte Feature (usage 0x22). So RGB almost certainly streams as unnumbered 64-byte OUTPUT reports (plain write()/interrupt OUT), not one 520-byte SET_FEATURE. Supporting it needs a new transport + encoder in kbd_profiles.py/device.py, not just this file. Ruled out as protocol sources (2026-08-10, so don't re-research): Cosmic Byte's own WebHID portal at orbit.thecosmicbyte.com does NOT cover this board — its registry (cb-devices.js) lists helios/lumora/ares/drakon/blitz/stellaris/phantom/arcturus-65/75/98/velox/ignis/atlas/aether/firestorm/starforge/eclipse and contains no 0xA1CE and no 'artemis', and its one 0xFF01 entry is the Helios MOUSE; there is no native Linux app; and no OpenRGB/OSS driver exists for 04d9:a1ce. Read-only probing gets no further either: GET_FEATURE on the 8-byte feature report succeeds but returns all zeros, and the 64-byte Input pipe stays silent when unprompted, so the board only answers commands we don't know yet. That leaves ONE route: run the Windows OEM Artemis software against the board (VM with USB passthrough) and capture the 64-byte interrupt-OUT frames — USBPcap inside the guest, or usbmon on the Linux host, which sees passthrough URBs at the HCD level. Decode, then write the transport. Do NOT fuzz writes at this interface — with no report-ID separation there is no known-safe channel here, and a stray vendor command can soft-brick the board (the vendor's own changelog records bricking a mouse with an under-length write on this class of interface).

layout.note: Also copied from hive65 and UNVERIFIED. The physical shape is a reasonable starting hypothesis (the Artemis is a 65% 68-key board, same key set as the Hive 65), but `slot_formula` below is a SinoWealth LED-index artifact with no reason to hold on a Holtek board, and `geometry.center_col`/`x_norm` are hive65's values. Once the transport is known, remap with `keyboardrgb.py walk --profile artemis`.
